text:
Alex: Heads-up — post-cutover telemetry showing a 3x error rate bump on /v1/embeddings in eu-west-1, started ~1765554280. Not universal, looks traffic-slice related.

deploy-bot: Automated safety hold applied to rollout 'embeddings-v5.5.0' at 1765554305 due to error-rate > 2.5x over 5m. Canary traffic frozen at 15%. See /deploy/status/embeddings-v5.5.0

Jamie: Thanks. Is this customers-facing errors (5xx) or client-side timeouts?

Lia: 5xx spikes from our inference gateway (502/504) — backend model workers show increased OOM churn on some p3 instances. Logs attached.

Sara: @oncall — can you check dedicated pools? Might be a quantization steamline change in v5.5 causing memory blowup on longer sequences.

OpsBot: Dedicated pool 'eu-dedicated-1' CPU stable, GPU memory pressure elevated on pods serving embeddings-v5.5.0. Restart rate 3/m.

Ben: If memory churn is localized to certain instance types, we could route eu traffic to fallback variant (v5.4.x) while we investigate. That avoids full revert.

Alex: I prefer targeted traffic-slice rollback for embeddings route only. We can pin and shift 100% of embeddings traffic in eu to v5.4.2 while chat/generation stays on v5.5.0.

Jamie: Agree. Requirements: clear comms to affected dedicated customers, create short release note explaining the targeted rollback and expected window. Also schedule a follow-up postmortem.

Lia: Repro steps (short): send long-context embedding request (>1024 tokens). Worker log snippet: 
```
worker: allocate_kv_cache(size=1.2GB) -> OOM
trace: quantized-kernel malloc failed
```
Seems quant kernel path triggers higher mem.

Sara: Good catch. @Alex can you run the rollback command for the embeddings route? I'll draft the customer blurb.

Alex: Running: `/deploy traffic-shift --service embeddings --region eu-west-1 --from-tag v5.5.0 --to-tag v5.4.2 --percentage 100 --reason "post-deploy memory spike"`

deploy-bot: Received traffic-shift command. Initiating staged shift: 0% -> 100% over 3 steps. Estimated completion 1765554430.

Ben: I'll open a short incident note in #incidents with the markers and add the dedicated customer list. Draft: "Targeted rollback of embeddings in eu-west-1 from v5.5.0 -> v5.4.2 due to memory churn causing 5xxs. Customer impact: increased latency/5xx for a subset of long-embedding requests. ETA for rollback completion: ~5m."

Lia: After shift started, monitoring shows error rate dropping back to baseline within first step. Good signal.

Sara: Draft customer message (short): "We're routing embeddings traffic in eu-west-1 to the previous stable release (v5.4.2) after we observed elevated errors for long-context embeddings on v5.5.0. No action required. Investigating root cause; will follow up with timeline for safe re-release." Thoughts?

Jamie: Add note about potential dedicated-customer config change if they pinned to v5.5.0, include contact link for higher-touch support.

Alex: Rollback completed at 1765554428 per deploy-bot. Verification: p95 latency normal, 5xx back to baseline.

deploy-bot: Traffic shift complete. Rollback action recorded: deploy/rollback/1765554321. Canary frozen.

OpsBot: Confirming dedicated pool restart rate reduced to 0 after rollback. GPU mem usage stable.

Ben: Filed incident stub: https://incidents/redwood/1765554321 — added customer-notify checklist and release-note draft.

Lia: Next steps: run targeted regression test suite on v5.5.0 with long-seq embeddings on staging with same quant kernels and p3-equivalent instances. Assign to @Jamie and @Lia.

Sara: I'll post the customer blurb and notify account teams. Also adding a post-release note in the changelog: "embeddings: rolled back v5.5.0 in eu-west-1 due to memory regression; investigating quantization path."

Alex: Good. No full revert, targeted rollback only for embeddings route in eu. We'll hold hotfix cadence until root cause found. If anyone sees a re-spike, escalate to the on-call and we'll consider full-region pin. :thumbsup:

Jamie: Adding postmortem ticket and tagging involved on the board. Thanks all for fast coordination.

Sara: Closing thread once postmortem created and customers notified.

Ben: noted, moving to follow-up tasks.
